chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

He is not regarded (as ready), the one who travels upon this road (to Makkah), if there are not in him three characteristics: piety that restrains him from disobeying Allah, and forbearance by which he controls his anger, and good companionship with those who accompany him.

key_terms.الطَّرِيقَ: The road (specifically referring to the journey to Makkah)
key_terms.حِلْمٌ: Forbearance or gentleness that controls anger
key_terms.وَرَعٌ: Piety or God-consciousness that restrains one from sin

ai.seo_question: What are the three key character traits a Muslim should possess before performing Hajj?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) emphasizes that spiritual merit in pilgrimage is contingent upon internal character rather than mere physical travel. He identifies piety (war') as the restraint from sin, forbearance (hilm) as the mastery over anger, and good companionship (husn al-suhbah) as the social ethic, reflecting the Shia focus on integrating inner taqwa with outward social conduct. This triad ensures the pilgrim embodies the moral ideal of the believer both in solitude and in community.
